findings.analysis: The substrate modified the boredom-vessel source both in the git working tree and inside the running container, without committing the change. The rationale (draft-gap-closing-activity needed scenarios that weren't present) appears operationally sound, but the method — in-place working-tree modification without a commit — is a governance gap: the change is invisible to git log and bypasses the normal commit-based audit trail. In S2 phase, the substrate is expected to author commits, not make uncommitted working-tree edits. This appears to be how the substrate 'hot-deployed' the change: write to repos/boredom-vessel/src/index.ts and docker cp to container, since boredom-vessel is one-shot (reads fresh on each fire). The substrate appears to have also updated agent-coordination.json to record the rationale, which is a positive governance practice — but the underlying code change is uncommitted.
